title: Typed Identity Meets Runtime Equality
finding: Canonical typed encodings do not prevent host-language dictionaries and sets from collapsing labels that compare equal.

counterexample.consequence: A state list can contain both labels while set/dict-based model structures cannot represent them independently.

mitigation: Reject equality/hash collisions between canonically distinct state labels before constructing the state-domain set; recommend distinct external canonical IDs.
limits: This is a Python model-representation boundary, not a mathematical or physical discovery.
Action-map collisions already erased during dict construction cannot be recovered by validation.
Regression tests were authored but not independently executed at artifact creation.
next_rung: CXLXVIII: canonical IDs as primary keys throughout the model API, or a formal restricted-label contract with adversarial tests.
